title: Boilerplate Field Replication (Trivial Structural Delegation)
pattern: Replicating multiple individual fields from a nested struct directly into a parent struct, and manually writing mapping logic to copy data back and forth.
why_bad: It introduces redundant state duplication and high boilerplate ceremony. Rather than using composition directly, developers are forced to replicate signatures, creating maintenance bottlenecks and risking synchronization decay.
detection: A parent struct containing a subset of fields with identical types and names as a logical sub-component struct, accompanied by manual field copying.
counterexample: DTOs that flatten complex object graphs to conform to external legacy API specifications.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Code Smells - Feature Envy"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 6.
